guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see a plausible case for Purdue staying more competitive than the market expects because its offense showed functional upside in the opener. Purdue produced 523 total yards, while Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns. We also place some value on Browne’s continuity as a returning starter, particularly for an underdog that may need to answer Notre Dame with sustained drives rather than rely on variance alone.

The concern for us is that Purdue’s opening performance came against Indiana State and featured 38 players making their Purdue debuts, including 16 first-time Purdue starters. The defense recorded three sacks and eight tackles for loss, but our broader numbers still point to major problems against a Notre Dame offense with advantages on the ground, through the air and in creating scoring opportunities. We can understand why our model is less pessimistic about Purdue than the market, but Notre Dame’s ability to attack the defense in multiple ways keeps that disagreement from becoming valuable enough for us to bet.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are focused on Notre Dame’s rushing offense against Purdue’s run defense. Our numbers identify this as the clearest path for Notre Dame to control the game: efficient rushing can create manageable downs, extend drives and repeatedly move the offense into scoring range.

For our Purdue position to remain viable, we need to see the front prevent early-down runs from turning into a steady stream of favorable situations. If Notre Dame consistently dictates terms on the ground, Purdue’s improved offensive showing may not be enough to keep pace with the margin the market is asking it to cover.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State and produced 523 yards of total offense.
Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State.
Fame Ijeboi led Purdue with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and added two receptions for 30 yards against Indiana State.
Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut against Indiana State.
Purdue committed no turnovers, recorded one takeaway and won the turnover battle against Indiana State.
Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown against Indiana State, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue is scheduled to host Notre Dame at Ross-Ade Stadium on Sept. 26, 2026; Notre Dame was ranked No. 4 in this Game 2 guide.
The Purdue-Notre Dame game is played for the Shillelagh Trophy.
Purdue lost 56-30 to Notre Dame in 2025, Barry Odom's only prior Purdue meeting with the Fighting Irish.
Against Notre Dame in 2025, Devin Mockobee took a handoff and threw a 14-yard touchdown pass back to quarterback Ryan Browne.

quarterback.fact: Ryan Browne is Purdue's returning starting quarterback and has started 15 career games for the Boilermakers.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and threw for 2,153 yards and nine touchdowns.
Browne has four career 300-yard passing games, including 317 yards in the 2026 opener.
Browne spent the spring of 2025 at North Carolina before transferring back to Purdue during the spring portal window.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed for the backup quarterback role; Meredith started at Northwestern in 2023 but had not played in the following two seasons.

offensive_personnel.fact: True freshman Brock Brownfield started the 2026 opener, becoming Purdue's first true freshman offensive lineman to start a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona was the only returning offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey appeared in 11 games.
Purdue added offensive line transfers Boaz Stanley, Nuku Mafi and Micah Banuelos; they entered 2026 with 21, 12 and five career starts, respectively.
The starting offensive line listed after the opener included Joey Tanona, Brock Brownfield, Boaz Stanley, Micah Banuelos and Nuku Mafi.
Purdue's running back room lost four-time leading rusher Devin Mockobee and added transfers Fame Ijeboi, Travis Terrell Jr. and Jerrick Gibson; Antonio Harris was the lone returning running back.
Thirty-eight players made their Purdue debuts and 16 players made their first Purdue starts in the season opener.

defensive_personnel.fact: Linebacker Charles Correa returned after starting all 12 games in 2025 and recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks.
Purdue added defensive linemen Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought a combined 81 games of college experience, including 60 at the Power Four level.
Transfer defensive back Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup in his Purdue debut.
Transfer linebacker Jojo Hayden started his Purdue debut and recorded four tackles and one tackle for loss against Indiana State.
Transfer defensive back Don Saunders recorded three tackles, one-half tackle for loss and a 35-yard interception-return touchdown in his Purdue debut.
Ian Jeffries recorded three tackles and one sack against Indiana State, while Trey Smith added one-half sack.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Zach Crabtree became Purdue's offensive line coach after coaching at Fresno State in 2025 and previously working with offensive coordinator Josh Henson at USC.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach during the 2026 offseason.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and was expected to miss the entire 2026 season.
George Burhenn entered 2026 healthy after an injury at Notre Dame ended his 2025 season; he caught two passes for 43 yards in the opener, his first game action in 349 days.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned after missing the 2025 season or most of it because of injuries.
Defensive lineman TJ Lindsey returned after being limited to three games by injury in 2025.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue surpassed 500 yards of offense against Indiana State for the first time since Oct. 12, 2024, at Illinois.
Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen for 2026, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.
All five Purdue players who scored touchdowns in the opener recorded their first points as Boilermakers: Tra'Mar Harris, Fame Ijeboi, Chauncey Magwood, Don Saunders and Asaad Waseem.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue held Indiana State to 12 first downs, the fewest allowed by Purdue under Barry Odom.
Purdue recorded three sacks and eight tackles for loss against Indiana State.
Purdue's defense allowed 284 total yards against Indiana State.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts and all five extra points against Indiana State, scoring 14 points.
Echeverria Lozano's three field goals against Indiana State were from 39, 27 and 25 yards and were the most in a game by a Purdue freshman since at least 1995.
Buffalo transfer Dylan Drennan punted once for 54 yards with a 49-yard net in his Purdue debut.
Xavier Townsend returned three punts for 24 yards against Indiana State.

series_context.fact: Notre Dame leads the all-time series with Purdue 61-26-2 and has won 10 consecutive meetings.

other_relevant.fact: Barry Odom is in his second season as Purdue's head coach and entered the Wake Forest week with a 3-10 record at Purdue.
Purdue named Ryan Browne, Charles Correa, Hudauri Hines, Jude McCoskey, De'Nylon Morrissette and Curt Neal its six captains for 2026.
